extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and informed readers of American politics and public administration; policymakers interested in constitutional and legislative design
extracted.subtask_description: A critical, fact‑based study of how the United States Constitution operates in practice with emphasis on where real power resides (especially Congress), the functioning of committees and caucuses, and the practical consequences for administration and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on functions rather than forms
rubrics_metrics.description: The great fault of political writers is their too close adherence to the forms of the system of state which they happen to be expounding or examining. They stop short at the anatomy of institutions, and do not penetrate to the secret of their functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate institutions by observing what they actually do in practice (their functions and effects), not merely by their formal descriptions or constitutional text. Anti-pattern: relying solely on 'literary theory' or canonical texts without examining contemporary practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare the 'literary theory' of the Constitution with its operation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Constitution in operation is manifestly a very different thing from the Constitution of the books. An observer who looks at the living reality will wonder at the contrast to the paper description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing constitutional arrangements, explicitly contrast doctrinal accounts (e.g., Federalist papers, textbook balances) with the actual machinery and routines of legislation and administration; identify discrepancies and their effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify the real centre of power
rubrics_metrics.description: The leading inquiry in the examination of any system of government must, of course, concern primarily the real depositaries and the essential machinery of power. There is always a centre of power: where in this system is that centre?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine who holds self‑sufficient authority in practice and through what agencies that authority speaks and acts. Example finding in the text: Congress functions as the predominant, controlling force in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess whether the Constitution remains adapted to its original purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: We are the first Americans to hear our own countrymen ask whether the Constitution is still adapted to serve the purposes for which it was intended; the first to think of remodeling the administrative machinery of the federal government, and of forcing new forms of responsibility upon Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether constitutional structures and administrative arrangements still serve their intended ends in light of changed circumstances (e.g., post‑war growth, expanded national functions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate the effectiveness of balances and checks (esp. state vs federal)
rubrics_metrics.description: All of these balances are reckoned essential in the theory of the Constitution; but the extent to which the restraining power of the States was relied upon ... has proved, of all constitutional checks, the least effectual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine whether formal checks (federal/state, House/Senate/executive/judiciary) operate in practice to constrain power. Look for evidence that some balances have been overridden or become ineffectual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine growth and adaptability of the constitutional system
rubrics_metrics.description: The Constitution is a corner‑stone, not a complete building... The growth of the nation and the consequent development of the governmental system would snap asunder a constitution which could not adapt itself to the new conditions of an advancing society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether constitutional simplicity and elasticity permit necessary institutional growth without loss of functionality; consider how statutes, precedent, and unwritten practice have expanded the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scrutinize Congress's relations with executive departments
rubrics_metrics.description: It can be discerned most readily by comparing the 'literary theory' of the Constitution with the actual machinery of legislation, especially at those points where that machinery regulates the relations of Congress with the executive departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate procedural and institutional interfaces (committees, oversight, appropriation power) where Congress shapes, controls, or constrains executive action in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess the role and consequences of the doctrine of implied powers
rubrics_metrics.description: That puissant doctrine of the 'implied powers' of the Constitution ... was the most formidable weapon in the armory of the Constitution; when Hamilton grasped it ... it quick[ly] constituted Congress the dominant, nay, the irresistible, power of the federal system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how judicial deference to legislative judgment about means and ends (implied powers) affects the expansion of federal authority and the erosion of state prerogatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge clarity of responsibility and public accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: When we shall have examined all its parts without sentiment, and gauged all its functions by the standards of practical common sense, we shall have established anew our right to the claim of political sagacity... single, unstinted power, and clear responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure whether citizens can locate who is responsible for policy outcomes; prefer arrangements that make responsibility direct and observable. Anti-patterns: dispersed authority, fragmented responsibility, hidden power centres.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare committee (Congressional) government vs responsible Cabinet (Parliamentary)
rubrics_metrics.description: The most striking contrast in modern politics is not between presidential and monarchical governments, but between Congressional and Parliamentary governments. Congressional government is Committee government; Parliamentary government is government by a responsible Cabinet Ministry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this typology to evaluate whether administration is driven by semi‑independent executive agents answering to committees (fragmented) or by a responsible collective executive accountable to the legislature (coherent). Consider consequences for coordination and policy planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate the committee system's effects on coherence between legislation and administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Despite the forcible and unnatural divorcement of legislation and administration and the consequent distraction of legislation from all attention to anything like an intelligent planning and superintendence of policy...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether standing committees and decentralized legislative routines impede integrated policy design and effective oversight of administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess caucus secrecy and lack of public accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: The caucus cannot be denied its power: it is shielded from all responsibility by its sneaking privacy. It has great power without any balancing weight of accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine the role of private party caucuses in pre‑arranging majorities and policy outcomes; consider transparency, publishability of debates, and how private prearrangement affects legislative deliberation and public oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check whether public opinion has effective channels and quick action
rubrics_metrics.description: Public opinion has no easy vehicle for its judgments, no quick channels for its action. Nothing about the system is direct and simple. Authority is perplexingly subdivided and distributed, and responsibility has to be hunted down in out‑of‑the‑way corners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess institutional mechanisms for translating citizen preferences into accountable policy (elections, committee selection, clarity of officeholder responsibility). Low accessibility is a critical defect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base analysis on present facts, not authoritative precedents
rubrics_metrics.description: It is, therefore, the difficult task of one who would now write at once practically and critically of our national government to escape from theories and attach himself to facts... striving to catch its present phases and to photograph the delicate organism in all its characteristic parts exactly as it is today.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological rule: prioritize contemporary empirical observation of routines, precedents, and administrative practice over reliance on canonical texts (e.g., Federalist) when evaluating government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize necessity of party cohesion mechanisms despite accountability costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Against the fatal action of so many elements of disintegration it would seem to be imperatively needful that some energetic element of cohesion should be provided... The wonder is that ... we have had, and continue to have, only two national parties of national importance or real power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging institutions, account for trade‑offs: caucuses or party discipline can provide necessary cohesion; however, weigh cohesion benefits against transparency and responsibility costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply practical common‑sense standards to institutional reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Gauged all its functions by the standards of practical common sense, we shall have established anew our right to the claim of political sagacity; and it will remain only to act intelligently upon what our opened eyes have seen...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate institutional proposals against pragmatic criteria: simplicity, clarity of authority, feasibility of implementation, and likely improvements in accountability and policy coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek fearless, unsentimental criticism as first step toward reform
rubrics_metrics.description: The first step towards emancipation from the timidity and false pride ... is a fearless criticism of that system. When we shall have examined all its parts without sentiment... we shall have established anew our right to the claim of political sagacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A normative criterion for analysts and reformers: adopt frank, dispassionate critique of institutions as necessary precondition to constructive change; avoid reverent or ceremonial deference to tradition.
